title: A Bird Under a Quarter Pound Stayed Aloft for 200 Days Straight
subject: alpine swift

scenes.text: One tiny bird stayed in the air for two hundred days straight.
Alpine swifts weigh less than a quarter of a pound. In 2011, scientists strapped sensors to six of them.
Three came back. Their sensors recorded no landing for more than two hundred days, over West Africa.
How? They eat insects drifting in the air, and they mostly glide instead of flapping.
Do they sleep up there? Nobody knows. Scientists suspect they rest in midair.
Two hundred days without a runway, and then they find their own nest again.

description:
One tiny bird stayed in the air for two hundred days straight.
Sensors on alpine swifts recorded no landing for more than 200 days, while the birds glided over West Africa and ate insects on the wing.
Could you go a day without sitting down?
first_comment: The sensors logged data every four minutes, so very brief touchdowns can't be fully ruled out. Do you think they really sleep in the air?
